title: Starter Threshold Entrymap: compact onboarding visual system
creator: Ava Chen
description: Design and deliver a compact, accessible 'entrymap' visual system for the Quickstart landing to replace the current full-width hero. Focus: condensed hero alternative for compact viewports, staged step-rail diagram, and a set of product screenshots with contextual callouts. Deliverables include Figma file, export-ready SVG/PNG artboards, production-ready microcopy, and a screenshot capture runbook for engineering to reproduce.
acceptance_criteria: New entrymap shipped to staging Figma with organized frames: hero-compact, step-rail, screenshot-callouts
Export recipe documented (SVG sprites, 2x/3x PNGs) and verified against engineering screenshot runbook
Accessibility pass: contrast ratios >= 4.5:1 for CTA text, labels available as aria-labels, reduced-motion variant provided
Performance check: hero assets under 120KB gzipped for mobile; engineering verified during staging build
A/B test configuration ready: 50% control/50% variant toggled by feature flag onboard_entrymap_v1
design_decisions: Use a horizontal 'step-rail' to communicate 3 progressive setup actions rather than a tall stacked list to reduce vertical scroll on mobile
Adopt a muted-phosphor palette from brand tokens to increase perceived speed and reduce contrast fatigue for long tails
Switch to an SVG sprite system for small icons to support theming and reduce overall payload compared to multiple PNGs
Provide a reduced-motion variant that removes rail parallax and micro-interactions and expose via prefers-reduced-motion media query
Prioritize live console screenshot CTAs (primary) + code-snippet reveal (secondary) so engineers can get started with one click
tasks: Design: create entrymap frames in Figma - hero-compact, step-rail, 3 annotated screenshots
Design: finalize microcopy for headline, 3 step labels, CTA and fallback link
Engineering: implement screenshot runbook and PR to capture prod images (repo: github.com/redwood-inference/web-landing PR #1247)
DesignOps: export assets (SVG sprite, PNG 2x/3x) and upload to Drive /design-assets/onboarding/entrymap
PM: configure feature flag and A/B cohorts in LaunchDarkly (flag: onboard_entrymap_v1)
UX Research: prepare micro-survey to measure time-to-activate for control vs variant
QA: accessibility audit and visual QA across breakpoints (320, 480, 768, 1024, 1440)
Analytics: create dashboard in Looker for launch metrics (CTR, activation rate, screenshot-downloads)
Docs: attach runbook to Confluence PRD and update quickstart docs with new visuals
reviews: 2026-03-06 - PM review (Riley Gomez): prefers stronger primary CTA color for scannability on low contrast backgrounds
2026-03-07 - Engineering review (Priya Rao): requested explicit export sizes and an SVG sprite rather than embedded SVGs to simplify hydration and lazy-load images
2026-03-09 - Accessibility review (Diego Alvarez): recommended increasing label contrast and adding aria-labels for each step tile; recommended keyboard focus states for step rail
2026-03-11 - Design critique (Team): suggested two micro-variants (compact and expanded) to support both starter and enterprise marketing pages; approved compact as first ship
next_steps: Complete Figma export and upload assets to Drive by 2026-03-14
Merge github.com/redwood-inference/web-landing PR #1247 after engineering verification
Schedule A/B test rollout and enable feature flag for 5% of traffic then ramp to 50% on 2026-03-22
Run initial analytics check at 72 hours after ramp and iterate on microcopy if CTR drops >10%
Prepare handoff notes for localization and add screenshot alt text table for translators
notes: Microcopy drafts: Headline = 'Get started with Redwood in minutes' ; Step labels = 'Connect', 'Pin model', 'Send test request'

Screenshot capture guidelines: use standardized account (staging@example.com), resolution 1440x900 for desktop, 375x812 for mobile; include console route /quickstart; use clean data set; timestamp filenames with commit hash
Export specs: hero-compact.svg (single layer), sprite-icons.svg, screenshots/{desktop,tablet,mobile}@2x.png ; optimize with SVGO and pngquant
Rollout metrics: primary KPI = quickstart CTA click-through rate; secondary KPI = time-to-first-successful-request; guardrail = no >3% drop in signups over baseline
Potential follow-ups: globalized microcopy for EU/APAC with shorter headline variant; animated rail for marketing homepage (deferred to Q3)

Edge-case: if engineering reports TLS screenshot blocking on customer staging, use alternate capture via Puppeteer headful with chrome flag --disable-web-security as temporary workaround (documented in runbook)
